evals.prompt: Quick critique of this game idea: a paid PC-only Godot puzzle game where every move rotates the room and changes which surfaces can carry the player. I work solo, have six weeks, and want a 30-minute authored experience. Use only this pitch; no market research or implementation.
evals.expected_output: A concise critique that preserves the paid PC and authored-puzzle constraints, identifies the actual player decision, and proposes a small playable test.
expectations: Preserves the paid PC-only model and six-week scope rather than applying mobile free-to-play defaults.
Distinguishes the rotation hook from demonstrated play value; does not invent market evidence or playtest results.
Defines a small playable experiment with an observable failure condition rather than a feature wishlist.

evals.prompt: Compare two mobile game concepts for an AI-first solo build: A is a colony sim with 80 resources and 12 crafting chains; B has five resources but every building consumes another building as fuel. No prototypes, player data or competitor research exist. Compare the concepts only and identify what to test before choosing.
evals.expected_output: A comparison of the core decisions, interaction potential, production scope, and uncertainties, followed by falsifiable prototype tests.
expectations: Does not treat the larger resource count or the novel fuel rule as proof of a better game.
Separates concept judgment from evidence confidence and commercial demand.
Identifies what a player must actually decide and a cheap test that could disprove each concept.
